svg.title: Post-flush: three structures, separate results
svg.desc: A completion circular queue holds BCB pointers. Under the BCB mutex the consumer may offer an eligible frame to a separate allocator waiter queue and per-thread pointer slot. It finishes old FLUSHING and walks that BCB linked waiter list to wake only flush waiters. A recipient separately checks a revocable offer.
svg.text: Post-flush: three structures, separate results
Verified mechanism at CUBRID f799e05; schematic, not a runtime snapshot.
1. Completion circular queue
flushed_bcbs: BCB pointers
Capacity: 8,192 pointer slots
Atomic producer / consumer cursors
2. Consume a pointer; hold that BCB mutex
Inspect current flags, fixes, linked waiters, zone and quota.
Only an eligible frame with a waiting recipient may be offered.
A consumed item is old work; eligibility uses current state.
3. Conditional offer to a frame allocator
Separate high / low queues store THREAD_ENTRY pointers.
Under the recipient entry lock: notify and publish BCB offer.
bcb_victims[thread index] stores the BCB pointer.
Linked waiters on one BCB
BCB.next_wait_thrd
THREAD_ENTRY.next_wait_thrd
READ → FLUSH → WRITE → FLUSH
4. Finish the old flush even without an offer
Clear old FLUSHING; preserve later DIRTY work.
Walk the linked list; remove and notify FLUSH waiters only.
READ / WRITE access grants belong to another helper.
5. Recipient locks the BCB and rechecks
Reject a revoked offer; otherwise continue protected reuse.
Queue-full fallback
No item was posted for this BCB.
Submitter finishes it locally.
This fallback makes no direct offer.
No page bytes in this queue; no new page I/O by post-flush; no guaranteed receipt.
Arrows show access or control flow; shared metadata still requires its own protection.
